clue.text: Magic feat by bowler, perhaps

explanation.surface: A conjuring trick performed with a bowler hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A conjuror pulling a rabbit from headwear performs one; in cricket a bowler taking three wickets with consecutive balls achieves one too.

clue.text: Wife appears to contribute to king's downfall

parts.note: to contribute is to help
in chess the king falls by checkmate, shortened to mate

explanation.surface: A wife seems to have played a part in a ruler's fall from power.
explanation.walkthrough: The royal downfall sounds historical, but the king is a chess piece and his downfall is checkmate.
explanation.definitionFit: A helpmate is an old word for a supportive partner, especially a spouse.

clue.text: Directed in West End play as a vehicle

indicators.note: in says the word for directed sits inside the other pieces
End beside West takes only the final letter of that word

parts.note: play, as in games, is sport
to have directed a business is to have ran it, so ran

explanation.surface: A London theatre production directed as a star vehicle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'West End play' suggests a London theatre show, but 'End' takes only the last letter of 'West'; 'in' puts the word for directed inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Transport is a means of conveyance, any car, bus or train that carries people.

clue.text: Top fruit in row

indicators.note: Top used as a verb means cut off the first letter of the fruit

parts.note: an orange is a citrus fruit

explanation.surface: The best fruit is displayed in a line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top' reads as an adjective (best fruit) but is a verb: remove the head of ORANGE.
explanation.definitionFit: A range of mountains or cookers is a line or series, a row.

clue.text: Meet to administer punishment

explanation.surface: An instruction to gather and dish out penalties.
explanation.definitionFit: Meet as an adjective means fitting or proper; and to discipline someone is to punish them for wrongdoing.

clue.text: Pace is frantic for the top places

indicators.note: frantic suggests wild disorder, so these letters are thrown into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: The pace is frenzied in the race for first place.
explanation.definitionFit: Apices is the plural of apex, a summit or peak.

clue.text: It contains part of the driving force

definitions.text: It contains part of the driving force

parts.words: It contains part of the driving force
parts.note: the force here is the constabulary, and the vehicle carries some of its officers on patrol

explanation.surface: Something holds a portion of the engine's power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Driving force' suggests motive power, but it is the police force out driving.
explanation.definitionFit: A patrol vehicle used by officers of the constabulary carries some of that force.

clue.text: Fashion is, as far as beauty goes?

parts.note: to fashion a garment is to cut it

explanation.surface: A remark that fashion goes only so far in creating beauty.
explanation.walkthrough: Beauty is proverbially only skin deep, so the skin is as far as beauty goes.
explanation.definitionFit: Cutis is the anatomical term for the skin, the layer beauty proverbially reaches no deeper than.

clue.text: Distinguished archbishop is turning up

indicators.note: in a down clue turning up reads the letters from the bottom upwards, a reversal

parts.note: Cosmo Lang was Archbishop of Canterbury from 1928 to 1942

explanation.surface: A notable archbishop is making an appearance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning up' reverses LANG + IS; Cosmo Lang was a famous Archbishop of Canterbury.
explanation.definitionFit: Signal as an adjective means notable or remarkable, as in a signal achievement.

clue.text: Cross some filthy bridges

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone is angry about some dirty bridges.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' looks like 'angry', but it is the noun: a mix of breeds.
explanation.definitionFit: A hybrid is the offspring of two different breeds or species, a crossbreed.

clue.text: To benefit from school, left to make a living

parts.note: to make a living is to earn money

explanation.surface: Leaving school to go out and make a living.
explanation.definitionFit: To gain knowledge from lessons is to acquire it through study, the profit of education.

clue.text: Monarch of the glen?

parts.note: the title of a famous Landseer painting of a majestic Highland stag; the monarch is a male deer, not a king

explanation.surface: Who rules over the Scottish valley?
explanation.walkthrough: The Monarch of the Glen is a Victorian painting by Landseer of a red deer with fine antlers in the Scottish Highlands.
explanation.definitionFit: A royal stag is a red deer with twelve or more points to its antlers, the regal creature of Highland glens.

clue.text: Soldier and maiden seek true entanglement

parts.note: M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

indicators.note: an entanglement is a tangled mess, so these letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A soldier and a girl look for real romance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'entanglement' scrambles SEEK TRUE to USKETEER, which follows M.
explanation.definitionFit: A musketeer was an infantryman armed with a musket.

clue.text: Conspirator having less of a case second time round?

annotationWithheld.why: Conspirator having less of a case second time round? (5): only reading is CAS + CA, CASE cut once then cut further on repeat, so 'case' and 'having less of' each do two jobs
annotationWithheld.clue: Conspirator having less of a case second time round?

clue.text: Considered admitting Eastender

parts.note: though can mean admitting that, conceding a point
read as East-ender: the end of East is T

explanation.surface: Someone thought about letting in a Londoner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eastender' suggests a Cockney from London's East End, but it is the end of 'East', T.
explanation.definitionFit: Considered and thought are both past tenses meaning reflected upon or judged.

clue.text: Preserved area from fresh strike

parts.note: green means fresh or new
to belt someone is to strike them

explanation.surface: A protected zone created after a new attack.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a ring of protected countryside around a town, where building is restricted, carries this name.
explanation.definitionFit: Land kept free from development around a city is protected, preserved open country.

clue.text: Month a military cop's on leave

indicators.note: on places the abbreviation for a military cop after the preceding letters

parts.note: Dec is the abbreviation for December
MP stands for military police, or a military policeman

explanation.surface: A soldier in the military police goes on leave for a month.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on leave' reads as a soldier's holiday, but 'on' places the military cop after the month and A, leaving 'leave' alone as the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To decamp is to depart suddenly, often secretly.

clue.text: Spy chief is showing suspicion

parts.note: M is the head of the Secret Service in the James Bond stories
giving can mean showing, as a dial gives a reading

explanation.surface: The head of intelligence is displaying distrust.
explanation.definitionFit: A misgiving is a feeling of doubt or apprehension.

clue.text: Not just a packet steamer?

parts.note: a packet was a ship carrying mail, so this ship carries more than one small parcel

explanation.surface: A vessel that is more than just a small steamship.
explanation.walkthrough: A packet steamer was a ship carrying mail on a regular route; 'packet' also means a parcel, which it carries.
explanation.definitionFit: A vessel carrying post between ports, the old packet ship, carries far more than one parcel.

clue.text: Foreign city, as spelt?

parts.note: read as an instruction, A followed in order by S makes the two-letter word as, so the clue word is spelt out letter by letter

explanation.surface: A city abroad, with the name spelt as it is.
explanation.walkthrough: Spelling the word 'as' letter by letter you say A, then S, which gives A THEN S.
explanation.definitionFit: The Greek capital is a city abroad from the British setter's viewpoint.

clue.text: Informal gathering causing upset in secular circles

indicators.note: in a down clue upset turns the letters bottom to top, so they read backwards

parts.note: laic means lay or secular, not clerical
O is a circle shape, so circles are Os

explanation.surface: An informal get-together upsets people in non-religious circles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' reverses LAIC + OS.
explanation.definitionFit: A social is a friendly party or get-together of a club or church.

clue.text: Shakespearian maid could return as femme fatale

indicators.note: return suggests going back, so these letters run in reverse

parts.note: a siren is a seductive and dangerous woman

explanation.surface: A Shakespeare character might come back as a seductress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could return' reverses AS SIREN. NERISSA is Portia's waiting-woman in The Merchant of Venice.
explanation.definitionFit: Nerissa is Portia's lady-in-waiting in The Merchant of Venice.

clue.text: Original toy, nonetheless, is only a trinket

parts.note: novel means original or new

indicators.note: read as none-less, the O for zero is taken from the word toy

explanation.surface: An original toy turns out to be just a bauble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nonetheless' reads as 'none less': remove O (zero, nothing) from TOY to leave TY.
explanation.definitionFit: A novelty is a small cheap ornament or gimmick sold as a gift.

clue.text: Proposition in article relative to Americans

parts.note: the is the definite article
sis is American slang for sister, a relative

explanation.surface: A proposal in a newspaper piece about US connections.
explanation.walkthrough: 'article' could be a newspaper piece, but it is the grammatical article THE.
explanation.definitionFit: A thesis is a statement put forward to be argued or proved.

clue.text: Keep heading north for port

parts.note: to keep something is to have it

explanation.surface: Keep sailing north to reach harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading' joins the pieces; the surface makes it a ship's course.
explanation.definitionFit: A haven is a harbour, a place of shelter for ships.

clue.text: Twelfth Night role played by musician

explanation.surface: A part in a Shakespeare comedy taken by a performer.
explanation.definitionFit: Viola is the heroine of Shakespeare's comedy; a viola is also a stringed instrument a player performs on.

clue.text: She appears at the front after being shot

definitions.text: She appears at the front after being shot

parts.words: She appears at the front after being shot
parts.note: the shot is a photograph, and the front is that of a magazine

explanation.surface: A soldier wounded in battle turns up at the front line.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shot' and 'front' suggest war, but she is photographed and appears on the front of a magazine.
explanation.definitionFit: A model whose photograph is printed on a magazine's front page.

clue.text: They could produce bouquet for some wines

explanation.surface: Grapes that might give a fragrant nose to certain wines.
explanation.definitionFit: Garden flowers can be gathered into a bunch of blooms; and rosé wines are pink ones.

clue.text: Defend no part of Lovelace's prison

explanation.surface: Protect something that is not part of a poet's jail.
explanation.walkthrough: Richard Lovelace wrote 'Stone walls do not a prison make' in To Althea, from Prison.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket to stonewall is to bat purely defensively; and Lovelace's poem says such masonry does not make a jail.

clue.text: I slog wildly for the county

indicators.note: wildly signals that these letters are flung into a new order

explanation.surface: A batsman hits out wildly for his county side.
explanation.walkthrough: SLIGO is a county in the west of Ireland; the surface suggests English county cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: Sligo is one of the counties of the Republic of Ireland.

clue.text: Humble dwelling you could get for a song

definitions.text: you could get for a song

explanation.surface: A modest house that you might buy very cheaply.
explanation.definitionFit: A shanty is a crude shack; it is also a sea song, so you get one when asking for a song.

clue.text: Nelson's was halved to secure agreement among crew

indicators.note: among puts the word for agreement inside the word for the crew

parts.note: a rowing crew of eight oarsmen is an eight
yes expresses agreement

explanation.surface: Nelson's fleet was cut in half to win consent from the sailors.
explanation.walkthrough: Admiral Nelson lost the sight of one eye; a rowing crew is an EIGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: Nelson was blind in one eye, so his vision was reduced by half.
